Lengua del pueblo ɨnkal Awá («gente de l: Language of the ɨnkal Awá people («people of the forest»), represented by the Awá Indigenous Unity (UNIPA). The Awá are one of the seven Indigenous peoples of Nariño.
La UNIPA elabora materiales bilingües (d: UNIPA produces bilingual materials (dictionary, conjugations, alphabet and teaching guides) to revitalize Awapit and keep ancestral memory alive. Content taken from UNIPA and Ministry of Education documents.
Lengua de la comunidad inga del Valle de: Language of the Inga community of the Sibundoy Valley; it is the northernmost dialect of Quechua.
Su sistema de numeración oral es decimal: Its oral number system is decimal and remains in use among speakers in everyday calculation and trade. There are Inga communities in the Sibundoy Valley, Santiago and the Yunguillo reserve (Putumayo). Content taken from academic studies and community booklets.
Lengua del pueblo Cofán, hablada en Putu: Language of the Cofán people, spoken in Putumayo and Nariño (Colombia), along the San Miguel, Guamués and Putumayo rivers, and in Sucumbíos (Ecuador).
Según UNESCO (2008) había 379 hablantes: According to UNESCO (2008) there were 379 speakers in Colombia and 600 in Ecuador, and the language is considered severely endangered in Colombia. The sources record a positive attitude towards the language. Content taken from linguistic studies.
Lengua del pueblo Nasa, presente en el d: Language of the Nasa people, found in the department of Cauca (Tierradentro). Yuwe means «mouth», «word»: nasa yuwe is «the language of the Nasa».
Los propios nasa explican que Nasa signi: The Nasa themselves explain that Nasa means «people» and that they think and name themselves through their language. The language is central to ceremonies and to transmission between generations. Content taken from sociolinguistic studies and Antonio Pito's research.
ɨnkal Awá: gente de la selva: ɨnkal Awá: people of the forest
Al llamarse ɨnkal Awá («gente de la selv: By calling themselves ɨnkal Awá («people of the forest»), the Awá describe their origin and their coexistence with other inhabitants of the forest and the universe, such as the river people (Pi Awá), the hill people (Put Awá) and the people of the first world (Ishkum Awá). Source: UNIPA Community Education Project (2019), p. 32.
El tejido de la higra y el canasto: Weaving the higra and the basket
Cuando una higra se completa, las tejedo: When a higra is finished, the weavers leave a thread called pãnchit tit («umbilical cord») to symbolize that life never ends. The elders teach that the Awá worldview is written in the basket: its holes are the «eyes for looking at the Awá world» (the rivers, the forests, the hills). Source: UNIPA PEC (2019), pp. 83-84.
Las lunas y el cuidado de la selva: The moons and caring for the forest
El calendario Awá distingue la luna clar: The Awá calendar distinguishes the bright moon (Kɨnaz Patapcha: waxing and full) and the dark moon (Tɨtnaz patapcha: waning and new). The elders say that in the bright moon trees and people are tender (Kuna) and in the dark moon, ripe (Sam); that is why cutting wood in the bright moon is not recommended. Source: UNIPA PEC (2019), p. 102.
Un sistema de numeración decimal vigente: A decimal number system still in use
El sistema numérico inga es decimal: las: The Inga number system is decimal: quantities above ten, one hundred and one thousand are built by combining the basic terms. It is fully in use among speakers, who use it in household economy and trade. Source: Chasoy, Montes, Hernández and Marmolejo, «La numeración en lengua inga», pp. 142-145.
Para aprender y calcular se usan cuerdas: To learn and calculate, people use colored knotted cords (yellow, red, white and black are the basic colors), seeds and counting boards. Each cord represents units, tens, hundreds or thousands. Source: Chasoy et al., p. 144.
El a'ingae se habla en Putumayo y Nariño: A'ingae is spoken in Putumayo and Nariño (Colombia) and in Sucumbíos (Ecuador). UNESCO recorded 379 speakers in Colombia and 600 in Ecuador in 2008; it is considered severely endangered in Colombia. Source: Fischer and Hengeveld (2023), p. 2.
Según Fischer y Hengeveld, la mayoría de: According to Fischer and Hengeveld, most speakers use fûe («one») and khuangi («two»), and sometimes khuanifûe («three»); from three onwards counting almost always uses Spanish loanwords. The other numerals come from Borman (1976). Source: Fischer and Hengeveld (2023), p. 19.
Antonio Pito explica que para ellos la p: Antonio Pito explains that for them the word Nasa means «people, here, with the people, minga, the same, the same ones, parts of the earth», and that they call themselves Nasa because they speak the Nasa language and think like Nasa. Source: Pito Nache (2001), p. 42.
Yuwe designa «labio», «boca» y «palabra»: Yuwe means «lip», «mouth» and «word». Each language is named with the group's name plus yuwe: nasa yuwe («language of the Páez»), mu yuwe («language of the Guambianos»); the wakas (non-Indigenous people) have their own language, wakas yuwe. Source: Ramos and Rojas (2005), p. 13.
Los sa’t y la lengua en la ceremonia: The sa’t and language in ceremony
Entre los roles de las autoridades están: Among the roles of the authorities are the sa’t («chiefs»), lifelong companions. Those who speak in the ceremony do so in nasa yuwe, since «language is unique for validating thought». Source: Ministry of Culture, Lenguas vivas, vol. IV, p. 83.
Territorio del pueblo ɨnkal Awá, represe: Territory of the ɨnkal Awá people, represented by UNIPA. The sau is the «Awá living space». No precise geographic location in the corpus sources.
Valle donde se habla el inga estudiado p: Valley where the Inga studied by Chasoy et al. is spoken. Other Inga communities: Santiago and the Yunguillo reserve.
Zona de los ríos San Miguel, Guamués y P: Area of the San Miguel, Guamués and Putumayo rivers, where A'ingae is spoken in Colombia; on the other side, the Aguarico River in Sucumbíos (Ecuador).
Tierradentro y comunidades nasa del Cauc: Tierradentro and Nasa communities of Cauca
Territorio nasa del departamento del Cau: Nasa territory in the department of Cauca. The Indigenous council members carry out the mandate of the gods in Tierradentro.
Habita en resguardos coloniales, resguar: They live in colonial reserves, Incora reserves and individual plots in the municipalities of Aldana, Córdoba, Cuaspud, Cumbal, Guachucal, Ipiales, Mallama, Potosí, Santacruz and Túquerres.
Se ubicó tradicionalmente en el municipi: They were traditionally located in the municipality of Pasto and in La Florida, Tangua and La Cruz, and in settlements in the suburban area of Pasto.
Pasto, La Florida, Tangua y La Cruz: Pasto, La Florida, Tangua and La Cruz
El pueblo Pasto, «los hijos del sol»: The Pasto people, «the children of the sun»
Los pastos son agricultores (papa, ulluc: The Pastos are farmers (potatoes, ullucos, maize) and recognize a dual origin: the first men were born from the marriage of Cumbal hill and La Bolsa lagoon. They have lost their language but identify as Indigenous and work on cultural revitalization. The 2005 DANE Census recorded 129,801 self-identified people.
El pueblo Quillacinga, «los hijos de la: The Quillacinga people, «the children of the moon»
El etnónimo quillacinga desapareció en 1: The name Quillacinga disappeared in 1940 with Decree-Law 1421, which declared the reserves non-existent. In 2009 the Ministry of the Interior recognized the Quillacinga community of Jenoy (Resolution 0050) as an Indigenous people.
Los quillacinga ya no hablan su lengua n: The Quillacinga no longer speak their native language: only traces survive in some place names and surnames, and researchers do not agree on its features or its language family.
En el tejido de la higra y del canasto e: The history and worldview of the Awá people are written in the weaving of the higra and the basket.
Luna clara y luna oscura orientan cuándo: Bright moon and dark moon guide when to cut wood, weave and conceive, according to the elders.
Sistema decimal con términos básicos del: A decimal system with basic terms for 1 to 10, 100 (patsa) and 1000 (uaranga), using knotted cords to calculate.
Los numerales propios se están perdiendo: The native numerals are being lost and from three onwards counting uses Spanish loanwords.
